newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM decides to spend New Year in a hotel.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM decides to spend New Year in a hotel.

text.p: With the Lima hostage crisis in its 10th day, Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto decided on Friday to forgo a traditional New Year's break in his home constituency and instead stay at a Tokyo hotel until January 3.

Government officials said Hashimoto would keep up his now daily routine of visiting a Foreign Ministry crisis operation centre, which has kept a 24-hour watch on the hostage affair at the Japanese embassy in Peru since the siege started on December 17.

Hashimoto also cancelled traditional guest-receiving at the Prime Minister's residence on January 1, and in a symbol of solidarity with the hostages, will not play golf, his favourite sport, during the New Year period, the officials said.

About 20 heavily armed Peruvian Marxist guerrillas are holding more than 100 hostages inside the Lima residence of the Japanese ambassador to Peru after storming into the compound during a packed reception.
Normally, Japanese prime ministers spend their New Year's holiday back in their home constituency.
Unable to travel home, Hashimoto opted to stay at a hotel to allow staff at the prime minister's residence to go ahead with their holidays.
For Hashimoto, it would have been his first new year's celebration at his home district of Okayama in western Japan since becoming prime minister in January 1996.
The New Year period, called "Shogatsu", is Japan's most important holiday season, when those living in cities travel in packed trains and jammed highways back to their ancestral homes.
